title: Change the engine oil and filter
summary: Drain the old oil, fit a new filter, refill with the correct grade and quantity.
interval: Typically every 10,000–12,000 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first. Long-life schedules can run longer but punish short-journey cars.
safety: Warm oil drains better but hot oil scalds. Run the engine a few minutes, then let it stand for at least ten.
Never work under a car supported only by a jack.
Used oil is a carcinogen and a pollutant. Wear gloves and take it to a recycling centre — pouring it down a drain is a criminal offence in the UK.

tools.name: Trolley jack and axle stands, or ramps
Oil drain pan (larger than the sump capacity)
Socket or hex key for the sump plug
Oil filter wrench or cap socket

parts.name: Sump plug sealing washer
parts.note: Single-use on most cars. A weeping sump plug is almost always a reused washer.

steps.title: Warm the engine, then let it stand
steps.detail: Five minutes of running thins the oil so it carries more of the sediment out. Then switch off and wait ten minutes before going underneath.

steps.title: Raise and support the front of the car
steps.detail: Axle stands or ramps on level ground. The car needs to be level when you check the level later, so note how you will lower it.

steps.title: Remove the undertray if fitted
steps.detail: Usually a handful of 8/10 mm bolts and plastic turn-clips. Keep the fasteners together — they are easy to lose and annoying to source.

steps.title: Drain the oil
steps.detail: Pan underneath and slightly offset — the first flow shoots sideways. Crack the sump plug, then undo it by hand and pull it clear quickly.
steps.warning: Do not overtighten the plug on reassembly. Sump threads are soft and stripping one turns a £30 service into a new sump.

steps.title: Remove the old filter
steps.detail: Canister type: unscrew with a filter wrench, it will be full of oil. Cartridge type: undo the plastic housing cap, lift out the paper element and replace the O-rings supplied in the kit.

steps.title: Refit the sump plug with a new washer
steps.detail: Clean the sealing face, fit the new washer, torque to spec.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.detail: Smear clean oil on the rubber seal before fitting. Canister: hand-tight, then three-quarters of a turn. Cartridge: torque the cap to spec.
steps.warning: A dry seal grabs and tears, and an overtightened filter is near-impossible to remove next time.

steps.title: Refill through the filler cap
steps.detail: Put in slightly less than the stated capacity, then work up to the mark. It is far easier to add oil than to remove it.

steps.title: Check level, run, re-check
steps.detail: Lower the car level, check the dipstick. Start the engine — the oil light should go out within a couple of seconds. Look underneath for leaks at the plug and filter, stop, wait a few minutes, and re-check the level.
steps.warning: If the oil pressure light stays on, switch off immediately and find out why before running it again.

steps.title: Reset the service indicator
steps.detail: Many cars have a button sequence to reset the counter; some need a scan tool. Skipping this only affects the reminder, not the engine.

steps.title: Take the old oil and filter to a recycling centre
steps.detail: Most UK household waste sites take engine oil free of charge. Seal it in the container the new oil came in.
